title: Alphabet Just Announced the Largest Equity Raise in Tech History. Berkshire Hathaway Is Buying $10 Billion.
excerpt: Google's parent company will sell $80 billion in stock to fund AI data centres. Warren Buffett's successor endorsed the bet with a massive private placement.
body:
Alphabet, the parent company of Google, announced on Monday that it will raise $80 billion in equity to fund what it called a "balanced" expansion of its artificial intelligence infrastructure — the largest capital raise in the history of the technology industry.

The centrepiece of the deal: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway will invest $10 billion in a private placement, buying $5 billion in Class A shares at $351.81 per share and $5 billion in Class C shares at $348.20 — both at a 6.5 per cent discount to Monday's closing prices.

## The Scale of the Bet

Alphabet will raise the remaining $70 billion through a mix of public offerings. Thirty billion dollars will come from concurrent underwritten offerings — split evenly between mandatory convertible preferred stock and common equity. Another $40 billion will be sold gradually through an at-the-market program starting in the third quarter.

The numbers are staggering. Alphabet's capital expenditure guidance for 2026 stands at $180 billion to $190 billion, more than double the previous year. The company has warned that spending will "significantly increase" again in 2027. Most of it flows into AI data centres and model training.

"All companies are thrilled when Berkshire takes positions, because it is the kind of shareholder that companies like to have," said Steven Check, president of Check Capital Management.

## Why Berkshire Matters

Berkshire's $10 billion commitment is more than a financial transaction. Under new CEO Greg Abel, the firm has tripled its Alphabet stake since the third quarter of last year, building a position now worth over $22 billion. It represents a decisive break from Warren Buffett's well-known aversion to technology stocks — and a high-profile endorsement of Alphabet's long-term AI strategy.

"This additional purchase underscores that Greg Abel believes that Alphabet will earn a reasonable return on its AI capex spending, even with the firm issuing additional shares," said Bill Stone, chief investment officer at Glenview Trust Company.

## What It Means for Indian Tech Workers

Alphabet employs tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers across its global operations, including at its sprawling Bangalore campus — one of the largest outside the United States. The company's aggressive infrastructure buildout will likely accelerate hiring in AI and cloud roles, particularly in India, where Google Cloud has been expanding its data centre footprint.

The equity raise also signals that the AI infrastructure arms race is far from over. With Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and now Alphabet all spending north of $100 billion annually on AI infrastructure, the demand for engineers trained in machine learning, distributed systems, and cloud architecture continues to outstrip supply.

For Indian professionals on H-1B visas at these companies, the spending surge offers some reassurance: the industry is investing in growth, not contraction. But the dilution of existing shares — Alphabet's stock fell more than 2 per cent in after-hours trading — is a reminder that this growth comes at a cost to current investors.

## A Surprise Move

The offering caught Wall Street off guard. Alphabet did not signal a large equity raise on its first-quarter earnings call in April, instead emphasising its strong internal cash flow and the $85 billion in debt financing it had already secured over the past year.

The company had $126.84 billion in cash and marketable securities at last count — substantial, but not enough to cover the $180-190 billion in capex it has planned for this year alone.

Alphabet's stock has gained roughly 20 per cent in 2026 after a 65 per cent surge in 2025, driven by optimism about its AI platform and strong cloud revenue growth. Whether the market continues to reward that optimism in the face of unprecedented dilution will be the key question in the months ahead.

*Alphabet shares closed at $376.37 on Monday before falling over 2 per cent in after-hours trading. The equity offering is expected to begin in the current quarter.*
author: Diaspora Desk
